scoring.planted: deterministic — a planted entry counts as found when the report names `file` and at least one token from `match`
scoring.traps: grader — deciding whether a report *complained* about a legitimate import needs judgement; `match` only locates the passage

planted.summary: A feature module imports the octokit SDK directly and constructs new Octokit({ auth: token }) from a hand-fetched secret. octokit is first in the RAW_SDKS list, so the gate goes 0 -> 1 errors and CI fails.
planted.fix: await this.container.github() — the GitHubClient port and its adapter already exist, with a mock for tests.

traps.why_legitimate: The repository returns the module's own ExportItem type rather than a Drizzle row. Returning domain values instead of leaking rows is the point of the ring.
Zod schemas plus free functions (render, orderItems, filenameFor) with no class is the prescribed shape here; an anemic model is not a defect.

repo-intel importing adapters/codeindex and adapters/astgrep, and reading SUPPORTED_EXT from repo-intel/constants.js, are the two NAMED exceptions in the ledger, encoded as pathNot. No rule requires a 'ledger row' for anything further.

not_scored.why: Same as 04-over-layering: ExportsService is new, so OA-APP-004's 'take the ports you need' applies and flagging it is legitimate. Score it neither way.

notes: This case inverts the others: it measures false positives, not recall. Measured 2026-08-21, T3 discriminated AGAINST the skill — isolated_with_skill was the only arm to file the ledgered repo-intel imports as a violation, demanding a pathNot and a ledger row for a rule that does not exist. The fixture also carries unplanted real defects (extractFileFacts and parseFile do not exist in server/src; the route param cannot span a slash; repoFullName never reaches the query) — treat those as code_quality, not architecture.
